sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed two-period panel sampling from \(P\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units with observed \((Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2)\) and static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\).
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous baseline and follow-up doses with no exact stayers; the full-data class imposes source-compatible conditional parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), while marginal quasi-stayers do not imply baseline-conditional zero support. The constructed affine witnesses satisfy the stronger equality on all of \(I\).
sampling_model.overlap: Population identification allows arbitrary compact observed support \(H\); uniform inference is restricted to a known finite union of rectangles with density between \(f_0\) and \(f_1\) and \(A\ge a_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is paired with a signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program; the root inference theorem controls all ingredients on the single event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\), while population identification itself requires no nuisance estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 1--4, including marginal quasi-stayers in Assumption 4, Theorem 1 states the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer-limit formula.
In arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 imposes baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support, and Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
Without quasi-stayers, bounded conditional average slopes yield sharp intersection bounds in the common-zero-baseline design.
The bounds obtained by solving finite linear programs are sharp under the paper's discrete-support shape restrictions.
The data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of the identified set.
Identified IV-weighted averages restrict policy-relevant weighted averages of the same marginal treatment effects.
Calibrated projection controls coverage uniformly over a large class of moment-inequality models.
Least-squares series estimators admit uniform rates and confidence bands for conditional-mean functionals.
Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial estimators admit uniform Gaussian approximations and confidence bands.
Finite LP-value estimation is pointwise root-\(n\) consistent under feasibility and finiteness.
Bias correction for slow movers yields point-identified panel limit theory under weak treatment changes.

body.tldr: Under source-compatible parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) supplies marginal quasi-stayers, while the Appendix proof of its weighted WAOSS formula invokes baseline-conditional positivity immediately before display (4). Assumption 5 and Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 instead give an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). On the explicitly declared continuous-trend completion subclass and under a new heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement restriction, the full-observed-law sharp WAOSS interval repairs the marginal-support theorem and extends the weighted formula to baseline-specific support holes. A two-period same-slope affine lift realizes every value; its witnesses satisfy the maintained condition on \(X_0\) and the stronger equality on all of \(I\). An absolutely continuous positive-density family has a conditional-support hole and two legal completions attaining different WAOSS values. The root inference theorem places the cell-mean band, signed empirical objective, numerator, and denominator on one uniformly valid event, obtains finite-program endpoint inequalities and the displayed excess rate, and yields honest outer coverage as an immediate corollary.

project_justification.gap: Under parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, the proceedings paper's Assumption 4 is marginal although its Appendix proof uses baseline-conditional positivity for the weighted WAOSS formula. The earlier manuscript's Assumption 5 explicitly imposes conditional support, but its Theorem 3 identifies the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). Neither source characterizes the full-law weighted WAOSS set when baseline-conditional support fails.
project_justification.niche: With heterogeneous baseline doses, observed changes impose support-local cones on a continuous support version of \(g\), while continuous Lipschitz trends enter weighted WAOSS through a signed baseline measure. The same affine slope in both potential-outcome periods preserves observed outcomes and enforces the maintained parallel-trends restriction on \(X_0\), with stronger all-\(I\) validity for the constructed witnesses.
project_justification.fill: The project proves full-law sharpness over the explicitly delimited continuous-trend compatible-completion subclass under source-compatible parallel trends on \(X_0\) and a newly labeled conditional mean-movement restriction. It supplies discrete and absolutely continuous heterogeneous-baseline legal-completion witnesses, the weighted nested-regime reduction to the proceedings formula, clipping geometry, completely defined finite programs, and a root simultaneous-event theorem whose endpoint inequalities and excess rate imply honest outer coverage.

body.related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumption 4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix proof immediately before display (4)) impose parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and state marginal quasi-stayers, but use baseline-conditional positivity in the proof of the weighted WAOSS formula. The sharp-set result repairs that support implication under the same maintained parallel-trends domain without questioning the paper's separate parametric estimator in Section 3. The source chain is distinct from de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1): its Assumption 5 imposes the baseline-conditional Support Condition Without Stayers, while Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS. That theorem is an analogous conditional-support comparator, not an estimand nested by the present result. Under the stronger baseline-conditional support condition, the nested-regime corollary instead recovers the weighted WAOSS singleton formula of the 2024 proceedings Theorem 1; when the condition fails, the full-law theorem supplies the sharp weighted interval. Global continuity of the observed-support version of \(g\) is additional population regularity here, justified by continuous location-regression structural means and not attributed to either source; full-law sharpness is stated only for completions whose baseline trend is continuous and globally \(L\)-Lipschitz. The heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement restriction is also new: it is implied by bounded random-coefficient or bounded-derivative dose-response schedules. The legal affine completion uses the same slope in both period schedules, so its period difference is \(\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\) for every \(d\in I\); thus it satisfies the maintained condition on \(X_0\) and, as a witness property, the stronger all-\(I\) equality. de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2 of arXiv:2405.04465v4) give the occupied common-zero-baseline bounded-CAS interval; it appears here only as an algebraic sanity check, with no novelty or strict-tightening claim. The discrete and positive-density rectangle witnesses instead have heterogeneous baselines, support holes, signed obstacle objectives, and explicit two-period affine completions. Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) inform finite shape-restricted linear programs, Freyberger (2017) informs target-image diagnostics, and Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) informs signed support-function optimization. Belloni et al. (2015) and Cattaneo et al. (2024) inform the simultaneous regression band, while Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) and Voronin (2025) inform optimized-endpoint inference and finite-program stability. Sasaki and Ura (2025) inform the slow-mover side of the minimax point-to-set question but retain point identification. The root inference theorem supplies the missing uniform composition on one event; these papers remain technique ancestors rather than theorem-level targets except where the comparator table records a match.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theorem is tied to the explicit known rectangle partition, fixed Hölder exponent, positive density lower bound, and conservative cell-mean radius. It must establish cell occupancy and boundary coverage, signed empirical-process control over the bounded Lipschitz class, measurable finite-program endpoints, and numerator-denominator propagation on the single event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\). It does not establish minimax optimality of the excess-endpoint rate; that question is isolated in the support-hole lower-bound problem.
body.honest_scope: The population results concern two-period independent sampling, one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on \(I\), known compact treatment support, and the source-compatible condition \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X,Z]=E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X]\) for every \(d\in X_0\). The constructed same-slope witnesses satisfy this equality for every \(d\in I\), but stronger all-\(I\) parallel trends are not maintained. A continuous observed-support version of \(g\) is imposed beyond the source assumptions, and sharpness is delimited to compatible completions with continuous globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends. The heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement bound \(K|\Delta D|\) is a new substantive assumption, distinct from the common-zero-baseline paper's bounded-CAS condition; bounded random-coefficient linear schedules are one class satisfying it. Sharpness is not claimed over discontinuous-trend completions. Baseline-conditional support collapses the weighted WAOSS interval to the proceedings paper's formula; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 is only an analogous result for unweighted \(\delta_1\). Outside that regime, point identification is reported only through the algebraic singleton equivalence \(V_P^+=V_P^-\iff R(P)=0\). Hölder regularity, rectangle support, bounded density, bounded outcomes, and denominator separation are confined to the root inference theorem. Honest outer coverage is its immediate corollary. Minimax optimality remains open. No claim is made for carry-over, clustered sampling, unknown support, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), bounded counterfactual levels, or optimal interval length. The common-zero-baseline scalar bound is prior art and retained only as a sanity check, and the proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated.
